means: The view a bird has: high above the scene looking steeply down, so the ground reads like a map.
does: Goes much further than "from above" - it is a SHOT SIZE change disguised as an angle. In the shot_cam_angle sweep the birds_eye panel pulled all the way out to the entire pitch with the character reduced to a speck, and shot.comp.perspective's overhead_map option did the same thing. Your character's face, costume and expression are gone. Know that before you reach for it. It is also inconsistent about height: the shot_angle sheet's birds_eye is an ordinary steep high angle over the shoulder, the shot_cam_angle one is a full aerial. Do not expect the same distance twice.
reach_for_it: when the geography IS the shot - a stadium, a battlefield, a city, a body alone in a large space. Never when you need a face.
used_in: shot.cam.angle birds_eye and the older shot_angle card; it overlaps shot.cam.height overhead/aerial and shot.comp.perspective overhead_map, which the project's own review flags as one instruction with three owners
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short dark hair, plain jacket, standing, city street, daytime
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
